skill.displayName: Lingxi-MindVault - Auto Memory Extraction for OpenClaw

llm.summary: The skill largely does what it claims (read local OpenClaw sessions, call the local OpenClaw agent to extract and write results to Feishu), but there are inconsistent metadata declarations and several privacy-sensitive behaviors you should understand before installing.

dimensions.detail: Functionality (reading local OpenClaw session files, calling openclaw agent, writing to Feishu multi-dim tables and docs) matches the skill description. However the registry summary shown to the platform claims no required env vars/config paths, while the included skill.json and SKILL.md require FEISHU_* tokens and use specific paths (e.g. /root/.openclaw/…). This metadata mismatch (declared none vs. required in files) is an incoherence that should be resolved before trusting the skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime scripts actively read all session files under the OpenClaw sessions directory, parse full conversation contents, construct an AI prompt, and instruct the agent to write extracted content to external Feishu services and send notifications. Reading and transmitting conversation contents to a cloud service is exactly the intended purpose, but it is highly privacy-sensitive: any secrets or PII present in sessions would be sent to Feishu. The scripts also instruct the agent/CLI to call Feishu-write tools — this will transmit data off-host.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No network download/install step is included; this is instruction-only with included shell scripts. The scripts rely on local binaries (openclaw, python3, bash, optionally inotify/jq per README). No remote archive downloads or execution of fetched code were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The required environment variables (FEISHU_USER_OPEN_ID, L2_APP_TOKEN, L2_TABLE_ID, L3_DOC_ID, L4_DOC_ID) are proportionate to the declared purpose of writing into Feishu. However there is a platform-level inconsistency: the registry metadata at the top claimed 'Required env vars: none', whereas skill.json and SKILL.md list these required credentials. Also the scripts expect to read a workspace/.env (session_check.sh sources it) and will inherit those secrets — ensure you supply only tokens for an account/space you trust. The script constructs prompts that reference the app token and doc IDs; this results in those credentials being used by the agent/CLI and therefore potentially exposed to any component that processes the prompt or agent output.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and is user-invocable. It asks the user to optionally add a cron job to run the session_check script on a schedule; that persistent run is configured by the user. The scripts create local files under the workspace and /tmp and manage locks; they do not modify other skills or global system settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to consider before installing:

- Metadata mismatch: The platform summary shows no required env vars, but the included skill.json and SKILL.md require FEISHU credentials and doc/table IDs. Do not trust the registry summary alone — inspect the included files (you did) and resolve the mismatch with the publisher or treat the declared required env vars as authoritative.

- Data privacy: This skill reads your full local OpenClaw session files and sends extracted content to Feishu. Do NOT install or enable it against a workspace that contains sensitive PII, secrets, or confidential conversation data you cannot transmit to the configured Feishu workspace.

- Use a test environment first: Create a dedicated test Feishu app/account and test workspace; supply tokens/IDs for that test account to verify behavior before using real production credentials.

- Keep credentials scoped and rotateable: Use short-lived or narrowly-scoped tokens for L2_APP_TOKEN if your environment supports them, and avoid using high-privilege global credentials.

- Review and run in sandbox: Manually review the two scripts (do_extract_and_write.sh, session_check.sh) and run them in a controlled container or VM that contains only non-sensitive sessions. Confirm how openclaw agent is invoked and whether any secrets appear in agent logs or external calls.

- Cron + persistence: The README suggests adding a cron entry. If you do so, ensure cron runs source your .env only from a secure location and that log files are protected. If you prefer manual invocation, do not add the cron.

- If you are not comfortable with automatic exfiltration of conversation contents to Feishu, do not install. If you proceed, limit scope by using test tokens/doc IDs and audit Feishu contents for unexpected data.
llm.findings: [pre-scan: none] expected: Static regex-based pre-scan found no signals. The scripts do call openclaw CLI and python, and perform file I/O and network-bound operations (writing to Feishu via the agent), which aligns with the expected behavior and therefore do not necessarily trigger simple regex rules.
